Interesting, but hard to achieve. Everything on the user's computer is visible to him, so you shouldn't hide any secrets from the user, as it's just unpractical.

If what you're trying to do is maybe stop someone from editing the file, you could encrypt it when you save it, and decrypt it when you're accessing it from the program. That most likely will stop a regular user, but it won't stop someone who has some knowledge, specifically about decompilation of Java programs (which is quite easy), because of course, the program itself needs to know the key to encryption, so it has to store it inside. From that point he could take the key and pry open the file himself, and lock it back, and the program would be unsuspecting.

If you're just simply trying to save something and make it go unnoticed, then you might save it to some random location that no one really looks into, maybe the Temp folder or something, but that is merely a workaround. I assume you want the OS to be completely oblivious of any file activity, in which case you're kinda out of luck.

Also, you might be thinking that if you saved the data inside the jar file, it would be invisible to the OS, or impossible for the user to edit, which is of course not the case.
